key_insight: Cryogenic s-SNOM can directly map how nanoscale strain alters exciton energies in monolayer WSe2, revealing that different strain-engineering routes produce very different local responses.
engineering_relevance: For strain-engineered 2D optoelectronic devices, the work shows that achieving reliable single-photon emitters depends on controlling not just strain magnitude but also damage, adhesion, and deformation mode.
method: Compared nano-indentation and patterned-substrate strain engineering in monolayer WSe2.
Used 9 K scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscopy to measure near-field optical response and topography simultaneously.
Correlated local exciton resonance shifts with strain model predictions at sub-diffraction resolution.
evidence_signal: The measured exciton energy shifts showed that nano-indentation produced strain more than an order of magnitude smaller than previously inferred, while pillar-based devices remained intact under more modest tensile strain.
watch_item: Interpretation depends on accurately separating true strain effects from puncturing, tearing, and adhesion-driven deformation in fragile monolayers.
paper_title: Nanoscale Mapping of Strain-engineered Excitons in Monolayer WSe$_2$
